title: Pasta Arrabiata
subtitle: Spicy tomato and garlic pasta sauce
excerpt: A fiery Roman pasta sauce: crushed tomatoes cooked fast with garlic, chilli, and olive oil. Angry, bold, and ready in 20 minutes. Penne or rigatoni are the traditional choices.

recipe.sourceNotes: Arrabiata, meaning 'angry' in Italian, is a classic Roman pasta sauce. It appears in Roman recipe collections from the early 20th century. The sauce is deliberately simple: only tinned tomatoes, garlic, chilli, and olive oil. There is no onion, no wine, no cream, and no cheese (though Pecorino Romano is sometimes served alongside). The chilli quantity is a matter of taste: the sauce should be noticeably hot. It is traditionally served with penne or rigatoni, whose ridges hold the sauce.

content.text: Cook the sauce at a brisk simmer so the tomatoes reduce and concentrate: low and slow produces a watery result. The garlic should turn golden and fragrant but not brown. Add the chilli with the garlic so the heat blooms into the oil. Adjust the chilli quantity freely: the sauce should have a real kick.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the garlic is golden and fragrant. Do not let it brown.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Season with salt. Bring to a vigorous simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 minutes until the sauce has reduced and thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the penne in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 150 ml pasta water. Drain.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce. Toss well, adding pasta water to loosen. Finish with flat-leaf parsley. Serve immediately.
